title: Prove it
desc: The What happened tab: In short, Worth a look, four figures, the map and the log behind them.
learningGoal: After this lesson you can turn a month of shield activity into one action and one sentence you are willing to sign.

steps.title: The tab that has to survive a question
steps.bodyMd:
Van Dijk Groep, a sixty-person installation firm near Zwolle. In March the board asks their office manager one question: **what personal data left our building last month?**

Overview and the four numbered steps of the Privacy Shield say what *should* happen. **What happened**, at the end of the path, says what *did*.

**Settings → Organisation → Privacy Shield → What happened.** The header reads "Each time the shield acted on a message, and every call your organisation made to an outside service.", with a period control offering `7 days`, `30 days` and `90 days`. It opens on **30 days**.

Two things to know before you read a single number. It is part of the Enterprise plan; without it you get a lock card, "See what actually happened". And if the shield is off right now, a grey line says so: you are looking at past activity.

steps.title: Two summaries, four figures
steps.bodyMd:
The tab opens with **In short**: the period in one sentence — how often the shield acted on a message, how many calls went to outside services, how often it replaced or stopped personal data — and a bar whose pills (*Replaced with placeholders*, *Stopped*, *Left with a tool, unchanged*, *No personal data*…) filter on that outcome. Beside it, **Worth a look** lists the findings.

Then four cards. They count different things, and mixing them up is how a report goes wrong.

- **Shield stepped in** — times personal data was replaced or stopped, split underneath as *replaced · stopped*.
- **Personal data found** — the finds, *in N messages and calls*.
- **Left with a tool, unchanged** — tool calls that carried personal data out as it was, with *of them outside Europe* underneath.
- **Stayed in Europe** — a percentage, not a count.

Every card is also a button: click it and the rest of the tab narrows to match.

steps.title: Which number moves?
steps.instruction: Four things happened at Van Dijk Groep on Tuesday. Match each one to the card on the What happened tab that it shows up on. Some move more than one card, but only one pairing uses every card once.

pairs.left: A quotation with a supplier's IBAN in it was stopped before the model saw it.
pairs.note: Stopping a message is the shield stepping in: it is one of the "stopped" under the card. The IBAN it found also counts under Personal data found.

pairs.left: In Ask mode, a colleague saw two customer names highlighted in the review dialog and pressed Send anyway.
pairs.note: The names were found, so they count. But nothing was replaced or stopped, so Shield stepped in stays where it was; In short counts it under Let through, and the log row reads Sent anyway.

pairs.left: An automation fetched a project file from the company's own self-hosted file server.
pairs.note: It is recorded like any other connected-app call. Your own server counts as staying home, so it adds to "own server" under the card and keeps the percentage up — and it is the only card it moves.

pairs.left: Twelve calls carried customer e-mail addresses to a server in the United States.
pairs.note: Personal data that left with a tool, as it was. The line under the card counts the twelve as outside Europe, and they pull Stayed in Europe down as well.

steps.title: A percentage, and what it leaves out
steps.bodyMd:
**Stayed in Europe** is written as a percentage. It is the share of calls with a known location that stayed on your own server or inside Europe (the EEA). The line under it shows the split: *own server · EEA · outside*.

A call to a service in Ireland counts as staying. A call to a server in the United States counts as outside, whether it carried personal data or not — which kinds left is what **Left with a tool, unchanged** is for.

Two kinds of call are neither in nor out: calls through a global network, where only the network's edge is visible, and calls to a server nobody could place. They are left out of the percentage and named under it as *not placed*. With no placed calls at all, the card shows a dash, not a flattering 100%. The map panel, **Where it went**, repeats the same figure.

steps.title: Worth a look: every finding that applies
steps.bodyMd:
**Worth a look** sits beside In short and lists every finding that applies, with the good news last:

- **"12 tool calls carried personal data out unchanged"** — with how many went outside Europe, the hosts that received most, and how many kinds tools hold back.
- **"A lot of your data is leaving Europe"** — when Stayed in Europe drops below **40%**.
- **"The shield is catching a lot of personal data"** — when more than **10** messages contained personal data.
- Calls through a global network, or to a server nobody could place.
- **"Nothing got past the shield unprotected"** — only when that is true.

Each finding has **Show these**, which filters the whole tab to its rows and reads *Showing these* while it is on. The tool finding also links to **Hold kinds back from tools**, the fix on What we look for.

steps.question: Worth a look at Van Dijk Groep reads "12 tool calls carried personal data out unchanged", and "12 of these went to a server outside Europe." What do you do first?

choices.label: Press Show these, then click one of the rows in the Log to open it.
Filter on Stopped and look for the blocked messages.
choices.feedback: Those are a different outcome. Stopped is what the shield did to a message on its way out; this finding is about tool calls that already left with personal data, unchanged.

choices.label: Switch the period to 90 days first, to see whether it is a trend.
choices.feedback: Worth doing afterwards. But the finding has already told you there are rows in this period, and widening it only mixes them with older traffic before you have read one.

choices.label: Go straight to Leaving your org and switch on "Use only AI hosted in the EU".
choices.feedback: Two things wrong with that. The switch sends chats to EU-hosted models, while these rows are tool calls, which follow the tool columns instead, so it need not touch them at all. And you cannot name the destination, the country or the kind of data in a report you sign if you never opened the rows behind the finding.

steps.explanation: Show these filters the whole tab to the tool calls that left unchanged. Opening a row in the Log gives you the tool, the country, who operates the server, the server address and the result, and the What we found column names the kinds of personal data. That is the paragraph you have to write, sitting in one row — and the finding's own link, Hold kinds back from tools, takes you to the fix.

steps.title: One log, every row behind the numbers
steps.bodyMd:
At the bottom sits the **Log**: every time the shield acted on a message and every call to an outside service, newest first, grouped by day.

Its columns read `Time · Person · Started in · What we found · What happened · Went to`. For a message, What happened is plain: Stopped, Hidden, Sent anyway, Placeholders, Search stopped, Noted only, Sent unchecked, Check failed. Started in is Direct chat, Agent, Automation or Notebook. Went to names the AI model, or the server a call went to with its location; a call that stayed home shows as *Your server*.

Click a row to see everything that was recorded. A call then names the tool, the country, who operates the server, the server address and the result, with how long it took.

Filters stack: a card, a day, a pin on the map, a person, a kind of data. **Show more** adds rows fifteen at a time, and the log loads at most two hundred of each kind: it is for reading examples, not exporting a month.

steps.title: From finding to signature
steps.instruction: Put the five moves in the order that ends with something you can defend. Drag them into place.

items.label: Read Worth a look at the top of the 30-day view.
Press Show these and open a row in the Log: country, operator, kinds of data.
Use the Started in and Went to columns to name the surface and the service behind it.
Change the setting the finding points to, then Save changes.
Come back a week later, same period, and read the same cards again.

sim.feedback: Finding, detail, cause, setting, recheck. Skipping the detail row leaves you fixing a guess; skipping the recheck leaves you claiming a fix you never measured. For tool calls the fix is one click away: the finding links to the tool columns on What we look for.

steps.question: After a demonstrably busy month, Van Dijk Groep's What happened tab shows Shield stepped in at 0 and Personal data found at 0. What is the right reading?

choices.label: Nothing yet. Zero is equally consistent with a shield that cannot see anything, so check Overview before you report it.
Good news: it proves no personal data was sent to any model last month.
choices.feedback: It proves nothing was recorded. A detection service that is not installed or not answering, or a How strict percentage set so high that almost nothing qualifies, produces exactly this same empty tab.

choices.label: The period is wrong; widen it to 90 days and report whatever appears.
choices.feedback: Widening the window is a reasonable check, but an empty 30 days after a busy 30 days is a signal in itself. Do not explain it away before you have looked at the configuration.

choices.label: Lower the sensitivity percentage until events start appearing.
choices.feedback: Turning the dial to make a report look busier is the wrong instinct, and it changes what is hidden from the AI for everyone in the organisation. Diagnose first.

steps.explanation: Go back to Overview. If the header pill reads Detection service not installed or not responding, nothing could be found. If How strict sits at a high custom percentage, almost nothing qualifies. If both look right, check that the shield was actually switched on during the period. An empty evidence tab is a question, never an answer.

steps.title: Close the one blind spot in the ledger
steps.instruction: Open the Privacy Shield and go to Leaving your org. Switch on "Check connected-app traffic for personal data", then press Save changes and wait for the confirmation. Every connected-app call is recorded either way, with its host, country and result; this setting is what lets those rows also say which kinds of personal data travelled with them. Without it, In short counts those calls as not checked for personal data.

steps.title: Why the operator console has no What happened
steps.bodyMd:
If your organisation runs its own server, an administrator can also reach a Privacy Shield editor through the platform console, where a picker lets them choose which organisation to edit.

That copy of the page shows Overview and the four steps. **What happened is deliberately missing there.**

The reason is worth understanding, because it is the same trap the rest of this course keeps pointing at. The monitoring figures are scoped to the organisation of the person signed in, not to the organisation chosen in the picker. Shown side by side with someone else's policy, they would look like that organisation's evidence while being your own.

So the evidence tab lives only where the two can never disagree: your own organisation's settings page. If you are asked for a report about another organisation, it has to come from an administrator inside it.

steps.title: Your turn: the paragraph you would sign
steps.instruction: Write the short paragraph you would send the board of Van Dijk Groep about last month. Use the 30-day view as your source. Name the period you read, give at least two of the four figures and say what each one counts, name one concrete finding from a log row (a destination, a country, a kind of data or a surface), state the one change you made and the date you will read the figures again. Then add the honest limit: one sentence on what this tab does not prove.
steps.placeholder: e.g. For 12 February to 14 March (the 30-day view), the shield stepped in 46 times: 40 replaced, 6 stopped...

steps.title: What you can do now
steps.bodyMd:
- **Read the four cards for what they each count.** Shield stepped in is replaced plus stopped; Personal data found counts the finds; Left with a tool, unchanged counts tool calls that carried personal data out as it was; Stayed in Europe is the share of placed calls that stayed on your own server or in the EEA.
- **Work a finding all the way down.** Show these, open a row for country, operator and kinds, name the surface and the service, change the setting the finding points to, then read the figures again in a week.
- **Treat an empty tab as a question.** Check the detection pill, the strictness and whether the shield was on before you report zero as a result.

ex-shield-org-evidence-board-note.title: A defensible month in one paragraph
ex-shield-org-evidence-board-note.task: Write the paragraph you would send Van Dijk Groep's board about last month's shield activity, based on the 30-day view of the What happened tab: the period, at least two figures with what they count, one concrete finding from a log row, the change made plus a recheck date, and one sentence on what the tab does not prove.
criteria: Names the period read (7, 30 or 90 days), so the figures can be reproduced by someone else.
Uses at least two of the four figures correctly: Shield stepped in as replaced plus stopped, Personal data found, Left with a tool, unchanged, or Stayed in Europe as a percentage of placed calls.
Cites one concrete log-row finding — a destination or country, an operator, a kind of personal data, or the surface (direct chat, agent, automation, notebook).
States one specific change made or planned, and says when the figures will be read again.
Adds an honest limit: the tab reports what was recorded, so it cannot prove that nothing was missed.
ex-shield-org-evidence-board-note.guidance: Pass a paragraph a non-technical board could act on and an auditor could reproduce. Do not pass an answer that treats a low count or an empty tab as proof that no personal data was processed; that confuses messages the shield acted on with tool calls that left; that quotes a figure without saying what it counts; that invents fields the tab does not show, such as message content or exported spreadsheets; or that ends without a change and a recheck. Invented numbers must stay consistent: the replaced and stopped counts must add up to Shield stepped in.

practiceTopic.title: Reading the Privacy Shield's What happened tab
practiceTopic.summary: How an org admin turns the shield's evidence tab into a defensible statement about what left the organisation.
facts: The evidence tab is called "What happened" and sits on Settings → Organisation → Privacy Shield, with the periods 7 days, 30 days and 90 days and 30 days selected by default.

The tab opens with In short (the period in one sentence plus outcome pills) and Worth a look (the findings), then four cards: Shield stepped in, Personal data found, Left with a tool, unchanged, and Stayed in Europe.

Shield stepped in is replaced plus stopped; Stayed in Europe is a percentage: the share of calls with a known location that stayed on your own server or inside Europe (EEA); calls not placed are left out.

Worth a look lists every finding that applies: tool calls that carried personal data out unchanged, a lot of data leaving Europe (below 40%), a lot of personal data caught (more than 10 messages), calls that could not be placed, and good news last.
Every finding has Show these, which filters the whole tab to its rows; the tool finding also links to Hold kinds back from tools on What we look for.

The Log has the columns Time, Person, Started in, What we found, What happened and Went to; clicking a row shows everything recorded, such as the tool, the country, the operator and the server address.
Show more adds fifteen log rows at a time, and the log loads at most two hundred rows of each kind, so it is for reading examples, not exporting a month.
The tab is offered only on the organisation settings page, never in the platform console, because the monitoring figures are scoped to the signed-in user's own organisation.

actionChecks.label: Turn on content checks for connected-app traffic
actionChecks.hint: Privacy Shield → Leaving your org → "Check connected-app traffic for personal data" → Save changes.

endpoints.returns: the organisation's shield config as a flat object with the boolean monitorIntegrations at the top level (false in the defaults used when no row was ever saved); :orgid is templated with the learner's own organisation id, and the handler only requires being signed in and a member of that org, so an org admin can always read it

criteria.label: Connected-app traffic is content-checked
criteria.hint: Privacy Shield → Leaving your org → switch on "Check connected-app traffic for personal data", then press Save changes and wait for the confirmation.
criteria.rule: GET /api/org-privacy-shield/<your org id> has monitorIntegrations === true
